explicit_propositions.text: The mother created a game called 'mother says' to teach children about choosing faith over fear.
In the game, children earned coins for following commands and could exchange five coins for a gummy bear.
When children reached four coins, they were challenged to give them up voluntarily, simulating a test of faith.
One child gave all her coins and received a quarter, allowing her to choose five gummy bears.
Another child initially refused to give up her coins and felt sad, but later received a coin to earn one gummy bear.
The mother used the game to illustrate the concept of trusting in a parent or God even when faced with uncertainty.
The mother later applied the same principle to real-life situations involving Evelyn’s fears, such as retrieving string and riding a bike.
Evelyn eventually participated in a peer game at school after being encouraged to choose faith over fear.
Repetition of the faith-over-fear theme across multiple contexts helped solidify the lesson for Evelyn.
A similar approach using scripted apology scenarios helped a younger daughter begin to say sorry despite initial resistance.
